{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings, deviations and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. The commercial architecture is largely acceptable to us: there is **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no employee non-solicit, no audit right and no liquidated damages or penalty running against Client**, and several provisions run in our favour (the § 6 vendor-side rate MFN and one-year cost freeze; § 2(a)'s express confirmation that we may acquire, develop or licence competing software). Our exit position is strong: § 14 gives Client a unilateral, no-cause termination right with run-off only to month-end and no exit fee, and § 13 renews in one-year increments on a 30-day mutual non-renewal notice. Governing law (California, San Luis Obispo County courts, §§ 26–27) sits at our fallback and is not redlined.

Six items require attention. Two are **outright gaps** — there is no post-termination transition assistance, data return or deletion mechanic anywhere in the document (material for a vendor that hosts our Web Site and holds borrower Credit Data), and no insurance provision at all. Four are **deviations**: the § 12 liability limitation caps TrueLink alone while our very broad § 12(a) indemnity is uncapped; TrueLink gives no non-infringement or performance warranty and no corresponding indemnity beyond breach of the Agreement; the § 2(a) licence excludes affiliates and contractors and § 15 offers no M&A successor carve-out; and § 15 conditions Client assignment on unqualified vendor consent.

Three of these engage playbook **walk-away** territory: the one-sided liability cap, the total absence of insurance for a vendor processing personal and credit data, and (at the edge) the consent-gated assignment prohibition with no successor carve-out.

**Process note:** the redline proposed for the limitation of liability finding did not pass verification and must be re-drafted and manually confirmed against § 12 before the markup is issued.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | Non-exclusive grant; § 2(a) confirms we may licence competing products. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No Customer-payable penalty or exit fee; § 5(a) minimums are ordinary pricing. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No restrictive covenant on us; the Non-Competition Agreement restricts TrueLink. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 14) | Client no-cause exit, no penalty; no Vendor convenience right mid-term. |
| **High** | **TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return** | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 14) | No exit assistance, data return or deletion; § 13 puts migration burden on us. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No Vendor audit or inspection right; better than preferred. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY (§§ 26–27) | California law and courts; sits at the fallback, mutual, not redlined. |
| **Medium** | **LICENSE — Licence grant scope** | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE | Grant runs to Client alone; no affiliate/contractor coverage, no successor transfer. |
| **Medium** | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY | TrueLink capped at 12 months' fees; Client uncapped. **Redline failed verification.** |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | Only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | Bounded and exitable; no shortfall or take-or-pay. Blank amounts to be completed. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No no-hire covenant; check the separate Non-Competition Agreement. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 13) | One-year renewals, 30-day notice; meets preferred position. |
| **Medium** | **WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration** | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only a Y2K warranty (§ 9); no services/conformance warranty or remedy. |
| **Low** | **ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY (§ 15) | No M&A successor carve-out; unqualified consent standard on Client. |
| **Low** | **INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 12(b) covers breach only; no IP infringement indemnity. |
| **Low** | **INSURANCE — Vendor insurance** | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance provision anywhere in the Agreement. |
| **Low** | **IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data** | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE | § 2(d) protects TrueLink only; no Client ownership of data or Support Services results. |

### Proposed redlines (deviations and gaps)

- **TRANSITION (§ 14):** insert six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter, carved out for retention required by law or by the System/Credit Repository Agreements referenced in §§ 1 and 13. Fallback of 90 days' assistance offered in the comment.
- **LICENSE (§ 2(a), § 15):** extend the grant to Client affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (affiliates addable on written notice at the fallback) and add a successor-transfer carve-out.
- **LOL-CAP (§ 12):** make the cap mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data-security breach, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap for both parties, and Client payment obligations preserved. *This drafting must be re-verified before issue.*
- **WARRANTY (§ 9 / § 12 disclaimer):** insert professional-and-workmanlike, conformance-to-documentation, compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties with repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy and an express carve-out from the § 12 implied-warranty disclaimer; 90-day services conformance acceptable as fallback.
- **ASSIGN (§ 15):** unqualified Client affiliate assignment right plus successor carve-out, reasonableness standard on consent, bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor, and confirmation that a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right. Fallback: mutual successor right on written notice.
- **INDEMN (new § 12(c)):** TrueLink IP infringement indemnity with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap. Narrowing our own broad § 12(a) indemnity remains a residual negotiation point, not part of this markup.
- **INSURANCE (new § 31):** CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback limits of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.
- **IP (§ 2):** reciprocal ownership clause — Client retains all rights in Client Content, Client IP and submitted data; Client owns Support Services deliverables and work product by assignment with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP; no joint ownership; expressly subordinated to the existing § 8(d) licence.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **One-sided limitation of liability (§ 12).** TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while our liability, including the very broad § 12(a) indemnity covering any breach, Client Content and third-party claims, is entirely uncapped. Capping the Vendor while leaving the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory under the rule; we require mutuality with standard carve-outs.
2. **No insurance at all.** TrueLink hosts the Web Site and transmits and processes Client data and credit repository information. The absence of any coverage requirement for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory; a new insurance section must be added.
3. **Assignment consent with no M&A carve-out (§ 15).** A consent-gated prohibition on Client assignment with no successor carve-out and no reasonableness qualifier sits at the edge of walk-away territory and must be corrected.
4. **Related material gap.** The absence of any post-termination transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation is a material gap for a hosting agreement given that TrueLink holds our data files (§ 2(f)) and § 13 places the migration burden on us; we should not sign without an exit mechanic.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-draft and manually verify the § 12 liability redline** before the markup is issued; this is the only proposal that failed verification and it is our first-priority commercial ask.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the four deviations and two gaps above, with the stated fallbacks in comments (90-day transition assistance; affiliates on written notice; 90-day services conformance; mutual successor right on notice; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
3. **Complete the blanks before signature:** the § 5(a) monthly minimum fees for Hosting and Support Services (to be set at or below expected run-rate) and the minimum Support Services period referenced by § 14, which should be completed consistently with our termination right.
4. **Fix cross-references:** § 14's "Subject to Section 4" and § 6's carve-out of "minimum monthly fees" by reference to "Section 4" appear to point to the Compensation section; confirm and renumber.
5. **Obtain and review the Non-Competition Agreement** cross-referenced in §§ 8(d) and 10(b) — it is not attached or defined here and may contain personnel non-solicit or data-use terms requiring separate assessment.
6. **Non-blocking asks** to raise if we are reopening commercial points: a Vendor renewal reminder 60 days before each renewal and a CPI/3% cap on renewal-term price increases (§ 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year only); optionally a neutral major California venue in place of San Luis Obispo County; and, as a residual point, narrowing our own § 12(a) indemnity.
7. **Confirm commercial appetite** on the three walk-away items so we know which, if any, the business is prepared to escalate."}
